content: The PPAN (Suppressor of SWI4 1 homolog) protein in humans is encoded by the PPAN gene. This protein is evolutionarily conserved and shares similarities with the yeast SSF1 protein and the gene product of the Drosophila gene peter pan (PPAN). The SSF1 protein is known to play a role in the second step of mRNA splicing. Both SSF1 and PPAN are essential for cellular growth and proliferation. The PPAN gene is co-transcribed with the P2RY11/P2Y(11) gene, which is located immediately downstream on the chromosome and encodes an ATP receptor. Chimeric transcripts that include sequences from both the PPAN and P2RY11 genes have been found to be ubiquitously expressed and are regulated during granulocytic differentiation. Exogenous expression of the PPAN gene has been shown to reduce anchorage-independent growth in certain tumor cell lines, suggesting a potential role in tumor suppression. Additionally, one of the introns within the PPAN gene encodes the small nucleolar RNA SNORD105.
